Subject: Clarify billing quantum & discount carve-out for SOW

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the draft SOW (attached). Before we proceed to execs, procurement and legal asked me to get a clear example of how Redwood will meter large streaming/long-context workloads and how the commit/discount carve-out would work if our usage falls short of the committed band. A few specific questions: 

1) Token rounding: for single streaming calls that produce long outputs (e.g., 20k–50k tokens), do you charge exact token counts or do you round each request to a quantum? If there is rounding, what is the quantum size?

2) Session behavior: when we maintain a long-lived session with KV/prefix reuse across calls, how is prefix reuse credited on the invoice? Is the reduction applied per-call or at the session aggregation level?

3) Minimums / microfloor: the SOW references a monthly minimum for burst pricing — how does that interact with streaming sessions that are sub-minute? Any per-session minimums we should expect?

4) Commit carve-out: OrbitCloud wants a simple protection for the first 3 months post-commit if actual usage ramps slower than expected. Can Redwood propose contractual language that results in a fair, easy-to-audit credit rather than a complex reconciliation?

I attached our suggested SOW redline (OrbitCloud_SOW_v3.pdf). Procurement also attached a sample invoice from Q2 for reference (sample_invoice_q2.csv) — you can use that to illustrate.

Can you provide a short example calculation and proposed clause we can give to our legal & procurement?

Best,
Emma

Hi Emma —

Thanks, got the SOW and invoice sample. Quick high-level answers below; looping in Karthik (metering) and Markus (legal/commercial) to add the exact clause and a numeric example.

- Short answers: we meter at request-level token counts but apply a billing quantum for invoicing (we round up to the nearest quantum per request). For streaming, each buffer flush is treated as part of the same request and subject to the same quantum rounding.

- Prefix/KV reuse: billed reductions appear as reduced input tokens on a per-request basis; when you maintain a long-lived session, the platform aggregates requests for reporting so you can see both per-request and session-level savings.

- Minimums: standard practice in the proposed SOW is a monthly committed minimum (monthly commit in tokens) and a small per-request microfloor to avoid extremely granular billing noise. Karthik will add the straight math and an example that references your Q2 sample invoice.

Next steps: Karthik — can you draft a 2–3 line clause for the SOW (simple true-up credit if usage < X% of commit for N months) and a worked example using OrbitCloud's Q2 numbers? Markus — can you propose wording that legal will accept (friendly to customers but protects the commit economics)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

— Monica

Subject: Re: Clarify billing quantum & discount carve-out for SOW — metering example

Emma / Monica / team,

Here is a concise, auditable explanation and a worked example using the Q2 sample invoice. I kept the definitions simple so your legal/procurement can follow. Happy to convert into a one-paragraph SOW addendum after alignment.

Key definitions
- Billing quantum: 512 tokens. Every request's billable token count is rounded up to the nearest 512-token quantum for invoicing (to limit line-item churn).
- Streaming aggregation: a streaming request that emits multiple flushes within the same logical request is counted once (total tokens emitted + consumed within that request) before quantum rounding.
- Session / prefix reuse: prefix/KV reuse reduces the billable input tokens on each request. Those reductions are recorded per request and reflected in the monthly aggregation.
- Microfloor: there is a per-request microfloor of 1 quantum (512 tokens) for any new streaming session under the default pricing. Customers can opt into a microfloor waiver for committed deals if agreed in the SOW.

Worked example (using round numbers inspired by your Q2 CSV):
- OrbitCloud example month: 1,200 streaming requests that average 3,450 billable tokens each (after prefix reuse). Raw token sum = 1,200 * 3,450 = 4,140,000 tokens.
- Per-request rounding to 512 quantum: each request rounds up to ceil(3,450 / 512) = ceil(6.738) = 7 quanta -> 7 * 512 = 3,584 billed tokens per request.
- Billed tokens = 1,200 * 3,584 = 4,300,800 tokens. Rounding delta = 160,800 tokens (approx 3.9% over raw).
- If OrbitCloud enabled a 'quantum-smoothing' feature (monthly aggregation rounding instead of per-request rounding), we would sum raw tokens first (4,140,000) and then round the monthly total to the nearest 512 quantum: ceil(4,140,000 / 512) * 512 = 4,140,288 -> only 288 tokens up, much smaller delta (~0.007%). This is an optional billing mode and commonly used for customers with very high request counts to reduce rounding overhead.

Minimums and carve-out wording (draft):
Option A — Simple 60-day ramp credit (recommended for OrbitCloud):
"If actual billable usage in the first three calendar months following the Service Commencement Date is less than 70% of the Monthly Commit, Customer will receive a one-time credit equal to 50% of the shortfall (i.e., (Monthly Commit - Actual Usage) * Contracted Unit Rate * 50%), to be applied within the next invoice cycle. This credit is limited to the first three months following the Service Commencement Date and is not applicable thereafter."

Option B — Monthly true-up (more conservative):
"If in any calendar month actual usage is below 70% of the Monthly Commit, Red­wood will carry a credit equal to the shortfall at the contracted unit rate and apply it to subsequent months, expiring after 6 months if unused."

Notes: the '70%' and '50%' numbers are placeholders; we can adjust based on the deal economics. The more customer-friendly A is simpler for legal and easier to administer. Option B is standard for longer-term commitments where credits roll forward.

Next steps: Monica/Markus — which option do we prefer? If you want the simplest path for procurement, I recommend Option A with an explicit 'quantum-smoothing' checkbox in the SOW so OrbitCloud can choose monthly aggregation rounding instead of per-request rounding.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Clarify billing quantum & discount carve-out for SOW — proposed commercial language

Emma —

Thanks for surfacing this. Monica/Karthik nailed the technical pieces. A couple of commercial asks / suggestions from my side so procurement has something redline-ready: 

1) Keep the SOW simple: include Option A (60-day ramp credit) as a one-paragraph addendum. It resolves the early ramp risk without complicated rolling credits.

2) Add an explicit checkbox in Section 2.3: "Quantization mode" with two choices — (a) Per-request rounding (default), (b) Monthly aggregation rounding. If OrbitCloud selects (b) we will apply monthly aggregation rounding and reduce rounding delta accordingly.

3) Microfloor waiver: include a sentence that for the duration of the committed term, the microfloor (1 quantum per new streaming session) will be waived provided monthly commit >= X tokens (we should set X based on the deal level; suggested default X = 10M tokens/month). Waiving the microfloor reduces per-request inflation for short sessions.

Suggested legal snippet (simple):
"Billing Quantum and Ramp Protection: Redwood invoices on billable tokens rounded to the agreed billing quantum (512 tokens) in the selected quantization mode. For the first three calendar months following the Service Commencement Date, if actual usage is below 70% of the Monthly Commit, Customer will receive a one-time credit equal to 50% of the shortfall as described in Option A. The Customer may elect monthly aggregation rounding in the SOW to minimize rounding delta."

Markus — please drop in final legal-acceptable phrasing; Monica — once we have final text I can circulate a single redline to OrbitCloud's legal. If Emma is fine, we'll update the SOW and send a one-page numeric example for their execs.

— Vanessa
